title: Training-Induced Escape from Token Clustering in a Mean-Field Formulation of Transformers
claim: Training makes the token distribution cluster early, stay clustered through the interior layers, then escape near the final layers.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right across layers, three shaded phase regions with sphere insets
description: A single wide plot with layer index t on the x-axis, from 0 to T. The y-axis is a distance to a clustered state. The plot is split into three shaded vertical regions: blue for Phase 1 Clustering, gray for Phase 2 Turnpiking, and tan for Phase 3 Escaping. Large phase titles sit across the top. Below each title is a black square showing a token distribution on a sphere, with gray arrows between them. The tokens start as a diffuse cloud, shrink to a tight point, then spread into a ring-like band. A jagged black curve shows the distance falling and then rising in a U shape. It is bounded above by a solid blue curve labeled Theorem 3.9 and below by a red curve labeled Proposition 3.5. Both the blue and red curves have arrows pointing to them from their labels.
caption: Overview of our results. The y-axis is an informal distance from the token distribution to a clustered state; in the analysis, the corresponding proxy is \(\Energygap\) in \zcref{sec:main}. Training can induce a phase of escaping from the clustered regime. The convergence rate from \zphasefromto{phase:cluster}{phase:turnpike} and the escape rate from \zphasefromto{phase:turnpike}{phase:escape} are approximately given in \zcref{rmk:rate_a,prop:one-step-escape}, respectively.
abstract: Transformers perform inference by iteratively transforming token representations across layers. This layerwise computation has been studied empirically, and recent mean-field theories of Transformer dynamics explain how attention can drive token distributions toward clustering. However, existing analyses treat model parameters as prescribed, leaving open how training reshapes this clustering picture. We study this question in a noisy mean-field Transformer in which only a parameter-linear FFN is trained under $L^2$ regularization. We identify a training-induced phase of the inference dynamics across layers: after clustering in the early layers, the token distribution can leave the clustered regime near the final layers. A single gradient-descent update already produces this escape, and minimizers of the training objective satisfy an exponential turnpike bound under which clustering persists through the interior layers. Our analysis is based on an entropy-regularized interaction energy that captures the clustering bias of attention, for which we establish a double-well landscape and a local Polyak-Åojasiewicz inequality. More broadly, our results point toward a training-aware mean-field theory in which training and inference dynamics of Transformers are treated together.
